notes.summary: Completion invariance of full semivaluations and primary ideals; qualified G331 gives equality of geometric completed C/D, raw envelopes, gauges, conductor and CE. No raw model-category descent claimed.
notes.detailedSummary: For every Noetherian local ring, exp(-v) gives uniform jet error exp(-N/r) and a homeomorphism of full normalized links including infinite values/nonzero supports. Completed primary ideals descend exactly. For excellent germs, G331 comparison on both rings transports geometric uniform cones and actual decreasing nets, hence all raw obstacles/regularizations, gauge cocycles and Jensen sets. Finite normalization and conductor commute by finite semilocal completion and a flat annihilator kernel. This is a complete scoped theorem, not universal envelope continuity.
notes.text:
## 1. Full semivaluations under completion

Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat R$ its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion, and $\mathfrak a$ a proper $\mathfrak m$-primary ideal. Semivaluations have values in $[0,\infty]$, are nonnegative on the ring, and have $0<v(\mathfrak m)<\infty$. No restriction on their prime support is made. Write $X_R=\{v:v(\mathfrak a)=1\}$. Choose $r$ with $\mathfrak m^r\subset\mathfrak a$; then $d=v(\mathfrak m)\ge 1/r$ on $X_R$.

For $v$ set $|f|_v=\exp(-v(f))$, with $\exp(-\infty)=0$. This is a multiplicative nonarchimedean seminorm with values in $[0,1]$. If $F\in\widehat R$, choose compatible representatives $f_N\in R$ modulo $\widehat{\mathfrak m}^N$. For $M\ge N$ their difference belongs to $\mathfrak m^N$: this uses the standard exact completion quotient $R/\mathfrak m^N\simeq\widehat R/\widehat{\mathfrak m}^N$. Thus
\[
 |f_M-f_N|_v\le e^{-Nd},\qquad
 \big||f_M|_v-|f_N|_v\big|\le e^{-Nd}.
\]
The second assertion follows directly from the ultrametric inequality: if the two norms differ, their larger value is at most the norm of their difference. Define $|F|_{\widehat v}=\lim_N|f_N|_v$. The limit is independent of representatives, and
\[
 \big||F|_{\widehat v}-|f_N|_v\big|\le e^{-Nd}\le e^{-N/r}. \tag{1}
\]
Representatives for $F+G$ and $FG$ can be chosen as sums and products of representatives. Taking real limits proves the ultrametric inequality and multiplicativity; $|0|=0$ and $|1|=1$. Define $\widehat v(F)=-\log|F|_{\widehat v}$, retaining the value infinity when the norm is zero. In particular this constructs, rather than removes, all infinite values and all nonzero supports. Units of $\widehat R$ have unit representatives and value zero. The same finite generators of $\mathfrak m$ show $\widehat v(\widehat{\mathfrak m})=d$, and similarly $\widehat v(\mathfrak a\widehat R)=1$.

Conversely every normalized centred semivaluation on $\widehat R$ satisfies (1), since $F-f_N\in\widehat{\mathfrak m}^N$. Its restriction has the same primary normalization and uniquely determines it. Restriction is therefore a bijection. Each completed norm evaluation is a uniform limit, on $X_R$, of continuous jet norm evaluations by (1). The map $t\mapsto e^{-t}$ identifies the compact extended interval $[0,\infty]$ with $[0,1]$. Hence every completed valuation evaluation is continuous in the extended-value topology. Both restriction and extension are continuous in the pointwise topologies, proving
\[
 E:X_R\overset\sim\longrightarrow X_{\widehat R} \tag{2}
\]
is a homeomorphism. No separability, normality, excellence, coefficient field, or metric on the link has entered this proof. Empty links cause no exception.

## 2. Exact primary descent and the geometric comparison gate

Every $\widehat{\mathfrak m}$-primary ideal $J$ contains $\widehat{\mathfrak m}^N$ for some $N$. Choose finite generators $F_1,\ldots,F_s$ and jets $f_i\in R$ modulo that power. Since $F_i-f_i\in J$, each $f_i$ belongs to $I=J\cap R$. Together with $\mathfrak m^N$, these elements generate an ideal $I'$ of $R$ satisfying $I'\widehat R=J$. Faithful flatness of completion gives $I'\widehat R\cap R=I'$, so $I'=I$. Thus $J=I\widehat R$. Conversely a primary ideal of $R$ extends to a primary ideal, as its finite-length quotient completes to itself, and contracts exactly. Units correspond too. The proof uses only primary ideals, and makes no assertion of descent for arbitrary ideals.

For every such ideal, $\widehat v(I\widehat R)=v(I)$, because its finite generators are in $R$ and all coefficients upstairs have nonnegative value. Consequently (2) identifies, exactly, every unit-or-primary profile, every finite nonnegative real combination of negative profiles, and their finite continuous uniform closures.

Now assume $R$ is excellent. Reduction commutes with completion: the completed reduction is reduced by the geometrically regular formal-fibre property, and the extended nilradical is nilpotent. Complete Noetherian local rings are excellent; completion of an excellent normal local ring is normal, using its normal formal fibres. These are ordinary completion/excellence facts at precisely these hypotheses, not conclusions about arbitrary nonexcellent rings. Alternatively restrict throughout to an excellent reduced $R$ whose completion is excellent reduced; the elementary conclusions of Sections 1–2 do not need these permanence facts.

The full G331 theorem applies separately to $R_{\mathrm{red}}$ and $\widehat R_{\mathrm{red}}$. On each it defines actual negative effective real Cartier presentations on actual primary blowups, tests their degrees on every contracted integral proper curve, and proves
\[
 C_{\mathrm{geom}}=\overline{Q_{\mathrm{primary}}}^{\|\cdot\|_\infty},
 \qquad D_{\mathrm{geom}}=\{\inf_i h_i:h_i\in C_{\mathrm{geom}},\ h_i\downarrow\}.
\]
The preceding exact profile transport therefore proves
\[
 E^*C_{\mathrm{geom},\widehat R}=C_{\mathrm{geom},R},\qquad
 E^*D_{\mathrm{geom},\widehat R}=D_{\mathrm{geom},R}. \tag{3}
\]
For the second equality transport the actual directed set and every term of each decreasing representation in both directions. There is no nested-net flattening, arbitrary infimum closure, or increasing completion step. Equation (3) is geometric positivity transport because of the independent G331 comparison on both rings. The topological primary statement alone would not prove it.

This proves equality of the completed geometric cones. It does not assert that their raw Cartier cores, their Cartier divisor groups, or their whole model categories are equivalent. No completed exceptional Cartier divisor has been assumed to descend. For context only, $\operatorname{Bl}_I(R)\times_R\widehat R=\operatorname{Bl}_{I\widehat R}(\widehat R)$ follows from flatness and the raw Rees algebra. Its full closed fibre is unchanged. Pulling back actual effective Cartier presentations preserves regular equations and their fibre-curve degrees. This supplies a direct core inclusion, but the reverse completed-cone equality in (3) comes from the proved comparison. Normality of arbitrary base-changed normal models and cofinal resolution are not needed by this route.

## 3. Envelopes, gauges, Jensen measures, and conductor after completion

For any function $f$ on $X_R$, including signed continuous, upper semicontinuous, and extended obstacles, form the raw supremum over $D$ minorants, with the empty-supremum convention $-\infty$. Transport of (3) gives the pointwise equality
\[
 E^*p_{\widehat R}(f\circ E^{-1})=p_R(f). \tag{4}
\]
The same equality holds for raw $C$ suprema. Homeomorphisms preserve both semicontinuous regularizations, continuity, and the existence of a greatest or maximal geometric minorant. Thus (4) transfers their existence and properties, and does not assume these properties universally exist. In particular the continuous-envelope property CE is equivalent for $R$ and $\widehat R$.

All primary gauges descend by Section 2. For a second primary ideal $\mathfrak b$, the common ray formula is $v\mapsto v/v(\mathfrak b)$ and $u_{\mathfrak b}(v/v(\mathfrak b))=u_{\mathfrak a}(v)/v(\mathfrak b)$. The denominator is finite positive continuous with a bounded inverse. Completion preserves it exactly, so (2)–(4) commute with this cocycle.

Normalization/conductor also commute at the level needed here. Let $R$ be excellent reduced and $S$ its finite normalization, with local centres $q$ over $\mathfrak m$. There is a regular conductor element $c$; $S_c=R_c$. The finite algebra $S\otimes_R\widehat R$ is the product of the completed $S_q$: the $\mathfrak mS$-adic and the Jacobson-radical-adic topologies are equivalent in a finite semilocal algebra, and the completed Artinian decompositions give this product. Each $S_q$ is excellent normal, so each completion is normal. Flatness keeps $c$ regular, and after inverting it the product algebra agrees with $\widehat R_c$. It is consequently finite, normal, and birational over the reduced $\widehat R$, and is its normalization. This proves the assertion without a smooth-model base change claim.

The conductor is $\operatorname{Ann}_R(S/R)$. Annihilators of a finite module commute with this flat base change: choose finitely many generators, express the annihilator as the kernel of the map $R\to M^{\oplus s}$, $a\mapsto(am_1,\ldots,am_s)$, and use exact flat tensoring. Therefore $\widehat{\mathfrak c}=\mathfrak c\widehat R$. The semilocal version of Section 1 identifies the normalization links and commutes with restriction. The finite-value conductor singleton stratum and the infinity-value quotient-fibre stratum are preserved, including their full nonminimal supports. G331's full-fibre-constant $C,D$ descent then agrees across completion. No conductor value has been divided to obtain a uniform error.

If $J_x(C)$ denotes the subprobability Jensen set, pushforward by $E$ gives exactly $J_{E(x)}(C_{\widehat R})$. Both the mass condition and every Jensen inequality transport through (3). Pushforward is a homeomorphism in the weak topology because continuous tests transport through a homeomorphism. Closed graph, upper and lower hemicontinuity, and the exact dual formula all transfer. This reduces the arbitrary excellent completion problem to the corresponding complete ring; it does not turn a complete ring into an algebraic germ of finite type over a field.

notes.summary: Complete compact-Hausdorff Jensen duality with subprobabilities and nets; CE iff weak lower hemicontinuity. Normal raw envelopes are zero or uniformly negative; general lower hemicontinuity remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: A Banach-cone separation proves raw p(f)(x)=min over positive Radon Jensen measures of mass at most one, with alpha>0 forced by negative constants. Closed graph supplies upper hemicontinuity only. Failure of lower hemicontinuity gives finite continuous tests, Euclidean convex separation and a convergent coefficient subnet contradicting CE. The actual G331 divisorial inequality rules out mixed-zero normal raw envelopes. These equivalent criteria do not close original P12.3.
notes.text:
Let $X$ be nonempty compact Hausdorff and $C\subset C(X,\mathbb R)$ a norm-closed convex cone of nonpositive functions, containing every negative constant and stable under finite maxima. Define $p_C(f)=\sup\{h\in C:h\le f\}$ for $f\in C(X,\mathbb R)$. A sufficiently negative constant is a competitor; hence $p_C(f)$ is finite bounded. It is lower semicontinuous. Negative shifting gives $\|p_C(f)-p_C(g)\|_\infty\le\|f-g\|_\infty$. If $D$ consists of actual decreasing $C$-nets, compact directed strict covers show its raw envelope agrees with this one: for $h_i\downarrow h\le f$, some $h_i<f+\varepsilon$ on all of $X$, and $h_i-\varepsilon\in C$ is a minorant. This is valid for nonmetrizable $X$ and arbitrary nets.

Put
\[
 J_x=\{\mu\ge0:\mu(X)\le1,\ h(x)\le\int h\,d\mu\ (h\in C)\}.
\]
Positive functionals and Radon measures are identified by the compact-Hausdorff Riesz theorem. The positive subprobability dual ball is weak-* compact; the inequalities make $J_x$ closed convex, and $\delta_x\in J_x$. The joint graph is closed since every $h$ is continuous. Its ambient product is compact, so this graph gives upper hemicontinuity: a contrary net of measures outside an open neighbourhood of $J_x$ has a converging subnet in that closed complement, contradicting the graph. This does not give lower hemicontinuity.

The exact formula, including its signs, is
\[
 p_C(f)(x)=\min_{\mu\in J_x}\int f\,d\mu.
\]
Consider the convex cone $W=\{(g,t):\exists h\in C,\ h\le g,\ t\le h(x)\}$ in $C(X)\times\mathbb R$. If $t>p_C(f)(x)$, the Lipschitz estimate places $(f,t)$ outside the norm closure of $W$. Hahn–Banach separation of a point from a closed convex cone supplies a continuous linear form $L(g,t)=\mu(g)-\alpha t$ nonnegative on $W$ and negative at $(f,t)$. Pairs $(r,-s)$ with $r\ge0,s\ge0$ belong to $W$, so $\mu$ is positive and $\alpha\ge0$. If $\alpha=0$, pairs $(-a,-a)$ force $-a\mu(X)\ge0$; positivity forces $\mu=0$, contradicting strict separation. Thus $\alpha>0$. Divide by $\alpha$. The same negative-constant pairs give $\mu(X)\le1$, and pairs $(h,h(x))$ give all Jensen inequalities. Separation gives $\int f\,d\mu<t$. Conversely each Jensen measure satisfies $h(x)\le\int h\,d\mu\le\int f\,d\mu$ for all competitors. Letting $t\downarrow p_C(f)(x)$ proves the formula, with attainment by compactness. The mass bound is at most one, not necessarily one. In the cone of all nonpositive functions the zero measure is allowed and ensures the zero envelope of a positive obstacle; $\delta_x$ gives a negative obstacle at $x$.

There is the exact equivalence
\[
 \text{CE for all continuous signed }f
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x\mapsto J_x\text{ is weak lower hemicontinuous}.
\]
If lower hemicontinuity holds, a weak neighbourhood of a minimizing measure where $\int f$ is less than $p_C(f)(x)+\varepsilon$ meets every nearby fibre. This proves upper semicontinuity of $p_C(f)$, while its raw supremum already gives lower semicontinuity.

Conversely suppose CE holds and lower hemicontinuity fails at $x$. There is $\mu_0\in J_x$ and a weak neighbourhood $U$ of it missed by fibres along a net $x_i\to x$. Choose finitely many continuous tests $f_1,\ldots,f_s$ and a Euclidean ball of radius $\varepsilon>0$ around $y_0=(\int f_j\,d\mu_0)_j$ whose inverse image is contained in $U$. The compact convex projections $K_i=(\int f_j\,dJ_{x_i})_j$ avoid this ball. A closest point $z_i$ to $y_0$ exists, and the squared-distance derivative at the minimizer gives, for $a_i=(z_i-y_0)/\|z_i-y_0\|$,
\[
 a_i\cdot(y-y_0)\ge\varepsilon\quad(y\in K_i).
\]
Take a subnet with $a_i\to a$ in the finite-dimensional unit sphere. All projected points are uniformly bounded, since the measures have mass at most one. Therefore for $f=\sum a_j f_j$ and all sufficiently late indices, every $\mu\in J_{x_i}$ satisfies $\int f\,d\mu\ge\int f\,d\mu_0+\varepsilon/2$. Duality then contradicts continuity at $x$, since $p_C(f)(x)\le\int f\,d\mu_0$. This uses a subnet, not a sequential compactness assumption on $X$ or on its measure space.

When $p_C(f)$ is continuous it belongs to $C$: local continuous competitors approximating it from below have a finite subcover, and their maximum is a uniform approximant in $C$. It belongs to $D$ iff it is continuous, because $D$ is upper semicontinuous and the raw supremum is lower semicontinuous. A maximal $D$ minorant is greatest by taking maxima with arbitrary minorants; it equals the raw supremum. These equivalences identify the remaining continuity obligation for the general geometric cone.

For normal germs, use precisely G331's normal-domain inequality: for each normalized centred divisorial $\nu$ there is $A_\nu>0$, independent of $g\in C$ and $v\in X$, such that $g(\nu)\ge A_\nu g(v)$. Its source qualifications, nonunit treatment and all-support density are part of the entire grant. If $f\ge0$, zero is a competitor and $p_C(f)=0$. Otherwise $f<0$ on a nonempty open set; divisorial density gives $\nu$ with $f(\nu)<0$. Every competitor satisfies
\[
 g(v)\le g(\nu)/A_\nu\le f(\nu)/A_\nu<0.
\]
Taking the supremum proves $p_C(f)$ is uniformly strictly negative. This does not make it upper semicontinuous and does not prove lower hemicontinuity. A mixed-zero nonnormal profile or an increasing energy spike is not a normal continuous-obstacle counterexample. Completion transports this dichotomy by n1.

The functional foundations used are ordinary Hahn–Banach, compact-Hausdorff Riesz and Banach–Alaoglu, with the finite-dimensional separation argument proved above. General weak lower hemicontinuity remains UNPROVED.

notes.summary: New formal trace-discriminant compatible Frobenius lift over a finite generically separable power-series normalization; Delta^q source precomposition. A single discriminant does not prove the isolated formal envelope theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: For perfect char-p k and complete normal R finite over A=k[[x]], with separable fraction-field extension, a trace-basis determinant Delta independent of q satisfies Delta R^(1/q) inside finite-free A^(1/q)tensor_A R. Free lifting gives every R-linear map a diagonal-compatible lift after output multiplication by Delta; the source multiplier in F_* notation is Delta^q. The completed-diagonal assertion additionally assumes k is the residue coefficient field. A ramified regular example gives v(Delta)=infinity on a nonzero support, so a primary compatible-multiplier ideal and BIG completed-diagonal product/restriction/subadditivity are still required.
notes.text:
Let $k$ be perfect of characteristic $p>0$, $A=k[[x_1,\ldots,x_d]]$, and $q=p^e$. Grouping exponents modulo $q$, with coefficient $q$th roots in $k$, proves uniquely
\[
 A^{1/q}=\bigoplus_{0\le\alpha_i<q} A\,x^{\alpha/q}.
\]
A series root is $\sum_\alpha x^{\alpha/q}\sum_\beta a_{q\beta+\alpha}^{1/q}x^\beta$; disjoint exponent classes give uniqueness. These are finite sums of formal series, so no unsupported interchange of infinite sums is involved. Rooting a finite $A$-module generating list for $R$ also makes $R^{1/q}$ finite over $A^{1/q}$ and hence finite over $R$. This proves actual Frobenius finiteness at the displayed hypotheses, not a Jacobian multiplier theorem.

Let $R$ be a complete normal domain finite over $A$, with $L=\operatorname{Frac}R$ finite separable over $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$. Choose a $K$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_n$ of $L$ with $e_i\in R$. Let $G=(\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(e_i e_j))$ and $\Delta=\det G$. The entries belong to $A$: they are in $K$ and integral over $A$, which is normal. The separable trace pairing is nonsingular, so $0\ne\Delta\in A$. This follows after extending to a splitting field, where the embedding matrix gives the nonsingular separable trace form; no nonzero value of $\operatorname{Tr}(1)$ is assumed.

Purely inseparable $K^{1/q}/K$ is linearly disjoint from the separable extension $L/K$. Hence $L\otimes_K K^{1/q}\simeq L^{1/q}$ and the same $e_i$ remain a basis over $K^{1/q}$. For $z\in R^{1/q}$, each trace $\operatorname{Tr}_{L^{1/q}/K^{1/q}}(ze_j)$ is integral over $A^{1/q}$ and in $K^{1/q}$, hence belongs to the normal $A^{1/q}$. Solving the linear trace equations with the adjugate matrix gives
\[
 \Delta R^{1/q}\subset\sum_i A^{1/q}e_i\subset A^{1/q}[R].
\]
Crucially $\Delta$ is independent of $q$. The multiplication map $P=A^{1/q}\otimes_A R\to L^{1/q}$ is injective: $A^{1/q}$ is finite free over $A$, $R$ is torsion-free over $A$, and its generic map is the preceding field isomorphism. Its image is $A^{1/q}[R]$. The displayed root decomposition makes $P$ a finite free R-module even if $R$ is not free over $A$ and is not Cohen–Macaulay.

For any $R$-linear map $\varphi:T=R^{1/q}\to R$, the containment gives an $R$-linear $T\to P$, $z\mapsto\Delta z$. Let $B=R\otimes_k T$ and $S=R\otimes_k R$. The module $P\otimes_k T$ is finite free over $B$. Multiplication $B\to T$ is a surjective $B$-linear map, with $T$ given its multiplication action. Thus multiplication $P\otimes_k T\to T$ lifts, by free-module lifting, to a $B$-linear map $\Psi:P\otimes_k T\to B$. Compose
\[
 T\otimes_k T\xrightarrow{\Delta\otimes1}P\otimes_k T
 \xrightarrow\Psi R\otimes_k T
 \xrightarrow{1\otimes\varphi}R\otimes_k R.
\]
Every arrow is $S$-linear and its diagonal restriction is $z\mapsto\varphi(\Delta z)=\Delta\varphi(z)$. Indeed multiplication after $1\otimes\varphi$ equals $\varphi$ after multiplication, by R-linearity. This proves a full compatible diagonal lift of $\Delta\varphi$, for every $e$. In the $F_*^eR$ notation the source precomposition is multiplication by $\Delta^q$, since $F_*r\leftrightarrow r^{1/q}$; it is not multiplication by $\Delta$.

For the completed-diagonal assertion additionally assume that $k$ maps isomorphically to the residue field of $R$, as in the intended coefficient-field setting. A finite set of maximal-ideal generators gives a presentation $R=k[[u]]/I$: successive homogeneous corrections represent every element modulo each maximal-ideal power, and completeness takes their series limit. The construction is continuous for the $(\mathfrak m\otimes1,1\otimes\mathfrak m)$ topology: each map is $S$-linear and sends the Nth adic submodule into the Nth one. The completion of $S$ is the Noetherian ring $k[[u,v]]/(I(u),I(v))$. Grouping exponents in the two variable blocks, then quotienting by the roots of the two defining ideals, identifies its root module with the completed tensor product of the two root modules. The original and root-adic topologies are cofinal, since a qth power multiplies each monomial degree by q. Multiplication and all maps extend uniquely; the commuting diagonal identity persists on the dense algebraic tensor submodules. The kernel of root multiplication is carried into the kernel of ordinary multiplication, so compatibility concerns the full root of the diagonal ideal, not just its ordinary extended ideal. No Noetherianity or general exactness of completion over the uncompleted tensor ring is assumed. Equivalently complete the finite free module and lift its basis directly along $\widehat B\to T$.

This theorem assumes an actual finite generically separable formal normalization. Cohen normalization over a coefficient field alone is not asserted to supply separability. No polynomial HH02 theorem was applied to power series.

The multiplier need not be primary. For $R=k[[t,y_2,\ldots,y_d]]$, $A=k[[t^n,y_2,\ldots,y_d]]$ with $n>1$ prime to $p$, the basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{n-1}$ has discriminant a unit times $(t^n)^{n-1}$. The finite map ramifies on $t=0$. A normalized semivaluation can kill t while another parameter supplies primary normalization, giving $v(\Delta)=\infty$. Therefore a single discriminant cannot supply the required uniform all-support primary bound. This is an obstruction to this inference, not a normal CE counterexample.

For a full isolated formal theorem one still needs a coherent ideal generated by compatible formal multipliers, unit on the full regular puncture of every actual primary model and hence containing a primary power in the isolated setting, and a BIG test-ideal product/restriction/subadditivity theorem on the appropriate completed diagonal with the exact all-map convention. Neither finite freeness nor the discriminant lift proves these statements. A continuous-Jacobian or Noether-different comparison would suffice only after its compatibility and BIG product/restriction statements are justified. Smolkin3.12 concerns reduced equidimensional algebras essentially of finite type over a perfect field; its tensor setting is not silently replaced. Its printed finite-field retraction is invalid and unused here.

CEMS Setting2.1 is broader: Noetherian F-finite normal schemes with dualizing complexes and compatible $F^!\omega\simeq\omega$, including essentially finite-type schemes over an F-finite local base. Complete equicharacteristic perfect-residue rings are F-finite by their power-series presentations and the root decomposition. Thus this source is not rejected merely for lack of field-finite-type hypotheses. Its big trace tails can apply once the actual dualizing data are chosen compatibly. Affine-base Koszul regularity also extends: on finite-dimensional projective Y over a Noetherian affine base, an ample globally generated A and vanishings $H^i(MA^{-i})=0$, $1\le i\le\dim Y$, propagate twists, give multiplication surjectivity and, by high-twist Serre generation, generate M. The generating Koszul complex is locally split, so no base-flatness is required. These facts locate the gap in the compatible primary multiplier and subadditivity mechanism.

The ordinary algebraic backgrounds used here are separable trace, pure-inseparable/separable linear disjointness and Noetherian completion. The new formal theorem is proved above. The full isolated excellent perfect-charp envelope theorem and general Jensen lower hemicontinuity remain unproved. Completion invariance from n1 gives an exact complete-ring reduction, not algebraization.

For finite continuous f, negative primary constants make the raw envelope finite. If h_i decreases to a D minorant, compact continuous strict tests h_i<f+epsilon select one index; subtracting epsilon gives a C competitor. Thus raw C and D envelopes coincide before positivity. Negative shifts prove nonexpansivity. Finite maxima approximate a continuous raw supremum uniformly, proving C membership. Conversely D membership makes the lower-semicontinuous raw supremum upper semicontinuous. Maximal minorants are greatest by finite maximum; a positive usc regularization remains below continuous f and hence equals the raw supremum.

The all-support J_k(f) inequalities define actual ideals, contain primary powers and survive integral dependence in the support-quotient valued field. J_kJ_l is contained in J_{k+l}; factorial divisibility makes their negative profiles increase. Rational density and negative shifts recover the raw supremum, with no increasing-D recognition. Decreasing-D closure uses insertion and one actual C net. On finitely many normal centres active branches stabilize on a tail; full-fibre-compatible masks descend by granted C descent. Strict continuous majorants form a downward-directed set by insertion and recover the target through compact-Hausdorff cutoffs. This avoids arbitrary nested-net flattening.
